chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Qasim from Aban from Mansur said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who made an oath of abstention (ila') from his wife, and four months passed. He said: 'He is kept in suspense (waiting); if he decides on divorce, she divorces him, and she has the waiting period of the divorced woman; otherwise, he expiates for his oath and retains her.'

key_terms.إِيلَاء: Oath of abstention from conjugal relations
key_terms.عِدَّةُ اَلْمُطَلَّقَةِ: The waiting period of the divorced woman

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a husband takes an oath to abstain from his wife for four months?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the procedural outcome of *ila* after the four-month period, emphasizing the husband's agency in choosing between divorce or expiation. It highlights the Shia jurisprudential view that the marriage bond remains intact unless the husband explicitly commits to divorce, thereby avoiding automatic dissolution. This ruling underscores the balance between enforcing the oath's consequence and preserving the marital union through *kaffarah* (expiation).
